TAIPEI (Taiwan News) — Defense Minister Wellington Koo (顧立雄) on Monday condemned China's planned live-fire drills in five maritime areas, saying the exercises create insecurity and that the military would closely monitor the situation.
China’s Maritime Safety Administration announced live-fire exercises in the Bohai Sea from Monday to Friday, the northern Yellow Sea on Monday, the South China Sea daily from Monday to Friday, and the southern Yellow Sea from Friday to Saturday, per CTS News. Military training is also scheduled in the East China Sea Tuesday to Thursday, with specific time windows varying by day.
Speaking before a Legislative Yuan meeting, Koo said the defense ministry had a comprehensive understanding of the situation in the Taiwan Strait, per Rti. The initial assessment was that they involved artillery units firing exercises along China’s coastal areas and posed a relatively low threat to waters surrounding Taiwan.
Koo said the ministry would continue to monitor Chinese military training. He condemned what he called the PLA’s “repeated exercises and military activities” across the Indo-Pacific, saying they warranted close attention.
The drills come as Japan's Self-Defense Forces and the US military prepare to hold their biennial Keen Sword exercise from Oct. 19-29. The Japan Times reports that the US military plans to deploy anti-ship missiles to Japan's Yonaguni Island, near Taiwan.
Asked about the reported deployment, Koo said US military deployments were based on local threat assessments and necessary operational requirements, per TaiSounds. He declined to comment on specific arrangements.
Koo also declined to comment on how other democracies might intervene in a conflict in the Taiwan Strait. He stressed that Taiwan's priority was to strengthen its defense capabilities and ensure national security.

FBI seizes Chinese hacker tools targeting Taiwanese infrastructure and universities
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-12
05:37:08 UTC
14:37:08 KST

TAIPEI (Taiwan News) — The FBI has seized scanning and phishing tools used by China-linked hackers to target Taiwanese universities and energy infrastructure, the US Department of Justice announced Thursday.
The operation has rendered the tools inoperable, according to the FBI, but experts warn that disrupting the campaign may not prevent the hackers from resuming their activities.
“Even if this company is sanctioned, it might set up another operation to start the same activities,” Wang Po-chi (王伯頎), an associate professor of criminal justice at Ming Chuan University, told PTS. “It may feel it has little to fear because the company might be based in one place, but the servers launching the attacks might be located elsewhere.”
The seized tools, known as Microscan and FishHub, were operated by hackers associated with Integrity Technology Group, a China-based cybersecurity company with government contracts, according to a press release by the US Justice Department.
Microscan, which scanned computer networks for vulnerabilities, targeted Taiwanese companies in the natural gas and power sectors, two Taiwanese universities, a US power company in South Carolina, airports in Japan and Poland, and an international non-governmental organization.
FishHub allowed hackers to gain remote access to targeted networks through spear-phishing and retrieve files to send to servers controlled by the Chinese company, the Justice Department said.
The FBI identified about 20 Taiwanese universities as confirmed victims of FishHub activity.
Chen Yun-nung (陳縕儂), a computer science professor at National Taiwan University, said malware can be difficult to detect when it operates through software already installed on a computer.
“The malicious program hides in existing management software and uses legitimate software for malicious acts,” Chen said. “For example, it can download and export your data, making it harder to detect because you will not see any additional programs running, just the original programs already there.”
The FBI said Integrity Technology Group, which was behind the major hacking campaign known as “Flax Typhoon,” is one of the companies helping the Chinese government “expand the reach and scale of its malicious cyber activity,” according to the press release.
The seizure is the latest US law enforcement action against the group, which the US Treasury Department sanctioned in January 2025 for its role in multiple cyber intrusions targeting US infrastructure.
In September 2024, the Justice Department announced an operation to disrupt a botnet of more than 200,000 internet-connected consumer devices infected by the company.

Details

Post-Tropical Storm "Rachel" is moving southwest across Southern California. The remnants of Storm "Rachel" made landfall over Baja California on Saturday evening, bringing strong winds and rain that caused flash flooding.
The remnants of Tropical Storm "Rachel," along with a separate storm system over the western United States, continued sweeping across the West on Sunday, causing flooding in several coastal communities in Southern California.
A combination of large ocean waves caused by "Rachel" and prolonged swells, partly caused by a Kelvin wave intensified by El Niño, resulted in significant flooding along the Southern California coast.
One of the hardest-hit areas was Newport Beach in Orange County, which has been experiencing flooding since Friday.
Major streets, such as Balboa Boulevard in Newport Beach and numerous adjacent streets, were inundated with floodwaters.
The city of Newport Beach declared a local state of emergency on Saturday in response to flooding caused by Tropical Storm "Rachel."

Human Rights Watch calls for end to Senegal LGBTQ crackdown ahead of Youth Olympics
- Human Rights Watch urged Senegal to stop its crackdown on same-sex relations before the Youth Olympic Games, saying it may breach the Olympic Charter and human rights rules.
- Senegal passed a law in March that raises the prison term for same-sex relations to 10 years, and dozens have been arrested, including 71 men sent to trial in August.
- HRW said the crackdown spreads fear and stigma, pushes people away from HIV care, and adds to wider erosion of LGBTQ rights across west Africa.
AI generated
DAKAR – Senegal should halt its crackdown on same-sex relations, which calls into question the country’s compliance with the Olympic charter ahead of hosting the Youth Olympic Games, Human Rights Watch said on Oct 12.
In March, the west African nation adopted new legislation doubling the maximum penalty for same-sex relations to up to 10 years in prison.
The deeply religious, predominantly Muslim country has experienced a wave of homophobia in recent months.
Dozens of individuals have been arrested on suspicion of same-sex relations, including 71 men who in August were referred to trial for “acts against nature”, a term used to refer to same-sex relations.
Senegal will host the first-ever Olympic sporting event on African soil when it welcomes some 2,700 young athletes for the fourth edition of the Youth Olympic Games from Oct 31 to Nov 13.
“The Olympic Charter prohibits discrimination on any grounds and commits host countries to respect human rights and human dignity”, HRW said in a report condemning the country’s “brutal crackdown”.
“The ongoing government crackdown on LGBT people raises serious concerns about Senegal’s compliance with international law, the Olympic charter, and Senegal’s own laws”, said HRW rights researcher Larissa Kojoue.
The crackdown is violating “rights, causing increasing fear and stigma, and should be ended immediately”, HRW said.
The rights group added that fear of arrest and stigma drives individuals into hiding and away from HIV testing and treatment, while also deterring lawyers from representing them.
Senegal’s law passed by an overwhelming majority in the National Assembly in March.
It also establishes criminal penalties for those found guilty of promoting or financing same-sex relationships.
LGBTQ rights advocacy is frequently denounced in Senegal as a tool used by Westerners to impose foreign values.
Several west African countries have enacted laws condemning same-sex relations in recent months, further eroding LGBTQ rights on the continent. AFP

EU eyes COP31 climate deal to accelerate CO2 cuts, document shows
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-12
05:05:57 UTC
14:05:57 KST

EU eyes COP31 climate deal to accelerate CO2 cuts, document shows
BRUSSELS, Oct 12 - The European Union will use next month's COP31 climate summit to push for agreement on a "package" of efforts to reduce the greenhouse gas emissions heating the planet, an internal EU document seen by Reuters showed.
Even as the world suffers extreme weather due to climate change, governments at recent UN climate talks have failed to agree to tougher action - with large emerging economies and fossil fuel producers concerned about the impact of such measures on their growth and development.
At COP31 in Turkey in November, the EU will push for a "mitigation package" focussed on reducing emissions, by turning countries' existing climate pledges into real-world actions, a draft EU document showed.
A key EU demand will be to extend until 2040 the segment in UN climate negotiations where governments discuss how to reduce emissions, and identify areas where more can be done, the document said. This negotiation track - known as the "mitigation work programme" - is due to expire this year.
The EU will also push for countries to respond to the UN's confirmation last month that the world will miss the 2015 Paris agreement's target to limit global warming to 1.5C, the document said. It was drafted by Ireland, which holds the EU's rotating presidency.
"We will look to strengthen our partnerships to deliver practical progress on global climate action, specifically on the transition away from fossil fuels and on electrification,” Irish climate minister Darragh O'Brien said.
EU climate ministers will discuss their COP31 strategy at a meeting on Monday.
Countries' efforts to address climate change have come under geopolitical pressure after the U.S. pulled out of global climate negotiations.
After last year's COP30 summit in Brazil ended without stronger commitments to rein in greenhouse gas emissions, EU diplomats say the bloc is planning a different approach for COP31 - attempting to avoid public clashes over contentious issues and instead focus on working with countries to implement their climate commitments.
The internal document said there is "no scope" for new climate funding commitments at COP31 - a position likely to put European nations at odds with poorer countries seeking more support. REUTERS

China sanctions Paraguay, Belize ministers over Taiwan ties
Unknown

China sanctions Paraguay, Belize ministers over Taiwan ties
Chinese foreign ministry cites national sovereignty and Taiwan separatist activities as reasons behind the measures.
China has sanctioned Paraguay’s communications minister and Belize’s foreign minister over ties to Taiwan.
The Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs made the announcement on Monday, citing the safeguarding of China’s national sovereignty and opposition to Taiwan separatist activities as the reasons behind the measures, which went into effect the same day.
The measures against Paraguay’s Communications Minister Gustavo Villate and Belize’s Foreign Minister Francis Fonseca include the freezing of their assets in China and the denial of entry visas to Hong Kong and Macau.
The sanctions also prohibit Chinese organisations and individuals from engaging in transactions, cooperation or other activities with the ministers.
The Foreign Ministry said that “certain anti-China politicians” who are “driven by self-interest” have pushed their nations to maintain diplomatic relations with Taiwan.
Beijing said the ministers had “taken a series of egregious actions and statements”, which are “damaging China’s core interests”.
Paraguay and Belize are two of 12 countries that maintain formal diplomatic relations with Taiwan.
China views Taiwan as its territory, a view the island’s government strongly rejects.
The measures come two days after Taiwan’s National Day celebration.
In a National Day speech outside the Presidential Office on Saturday, Taiwan President William Lai Ching-te said the island “cherishes peace” and will “not give up our freedom”.
China’s Taiwan Affairs Office condemned Lai’s speech, saying it “disregards facts, distorts the truth, misleads the public, and reveals ulterior motives”.
In January, Chinese President Xi Jinping pledged to achieve the “reunification” of China and Taiwan, calling the goal “unstoppable”.
Diplomatic relations
Paraguay’s Communications Minister Villate marked Taiwan’s National Day with a social media post, saying: “Paraguay reaffirms its relationship of friendship and cooperation, based on shared values and principles: the self-determination of peoples, human rights and democracy.”
The Belize embassy in Taiwan also posted a message on its Facebook celebrating the 37th anniversary of their diplomatic relations.
“Together, we look forward to a future of growth, opportunity, and lasting friendship,” the embassy wrote.
Last month, Taiwan’s Foreign Minister Lin Chia-lung visited Belize. His ministry said the two sides had agreed to deepen ties.
Taiwan’s other allies in the Americas include Guatemala and Haiti. It also has formal diplomatic ties with three Caribbean islands.
The United States does not have formal diplomatic ties with Taiwan, but Washington is bound by law to provide the island with the means to defend itself.
Earlier this month, the US delivered two fighter jets to Taiwan as the island seeks to build its defence capabilities to deter a feared attack from China.

US launches Section 337 probe involving Taiwan's Foxconn, Delta, Quanta
Unknown

2026-10-12
04:48:24 UTC
13:48:24 KST

TAIPEI (Taiwan News) — The US International Trade Commission (USITC) on Friday launched a patent investigation involving Taiwan tech manufacturers Foxconn, Delta Electronics, and Quanta Computer.
The commission said it voted to investigate alleged patent infringement involving vertical power delivery systems, related components, and computing systems containing the technology. The case is being conducted under Section 337 of the Tariff Act of 1930, which addresses unfair practices involving imported products.
The investigation stems from a Sept. 9 complaint by US power technology company Vicor Corp., which was supplemented the following day. Vicor alleges that the importation and sale of the products in the US infringe its patents and is seeking an order barring infringing products from entering the country, orders requiring the respondents to stop selling them, and a bond on affected imports during the 60-day presidential review period.
The respondents include Foxconn and its affiliates, Delta Electronics and its US subsidiaries, and Quanta Computer, Quanta Cloud Technology, and their US affiliates. Other respondents include Germany's Infineon Technologies, US-based Monolithic Power Systems, Flex, and Canada's Celestica, as well as Chinese subsidiaries of several companies.
The USITC's chief administrative law judge will assign the case to an administrative law judge, who will schedule an evidentiary hearing and issue an initial determination on whether Section 337 was violated. The commission may review that determination and set a target date to complete the investigation within 45 days of its launch.
The Ministry of Economic Affairs said Section 337 investigations typically take 12 to 16 months to complete, per Newtalk. If Vicor prevails, the commission could restrict affected products from entering the US market or order companies to stop selling them.
The ministry said the dispute concerns patent rights between private companies and remains under review. The government will monitor developments, maintain contact with the companies involved, and provide appropriate assistance if necessary.
Delta Electronics said it takes intellectual property rights and compliance with local laws seriously and would respond through the relevant legal procedures to protect its interests, Newtalk reported. The company said the investigation had not affected its products and declined to comment further while the proceedings were underway.

TAIPEI (Taiwan News) — A domestic tourism subsidy program used 26% of its weekday accommodation budget in its first month, with the Tourism Administration saying it spent more than NT$390 million (US$12 million) on discounts for over 400,000 room nights nationwide.
Hualien, Taitung, Yilan, Pingtung, and Tainan were the five most popular destinations based on the number of subsidized room nights, Tourism Administration Deputy Director Huang Ho-ting (黃荷婷) said, per CNA.
The program indicates strong demand for travel to eastern Taiwan, where local governments have also introduced additional incentives to encourage visitors to stay longer. Hualien offers eligible independent travelers additional accommodation subsidies up to NT$7,000, while Taitung offers incentives for longer stays and travel to offshore islands.
Initially scheduled to run until Nov. 30, authorities reserve the right to announce early termination of the program two weeks in advance if available funding is close to being exhausted. There are currently no plans to add funding, Huang said, adding that the administration would review the program's performance on a rolling basis.
Under the weekday accommodation scheme, eligible travelers staying at participating licensed hotels and guesthouses from Sunday through Thursday can receive discounts of up to NT$2,000 for two consecutive nights. The first night is eligible for a discount of up to NT$800, and the second up to NT$1,200. On offshore islands, the maximum combined discount is NT$2,500.
The program excludes national holidays and consecutive holiday periods. Travelers can stay at different participating properties for the two nights, provided the stays are consecutive and meet the program's requirements.
The administration also introduced a birthday accommodation voucher scheme. A total of 12,000 people were selected in September, with 1,000 winners for each birth month receiving NT$1,200 in accommodation subsidies. The birthday benefit can be combined with the weekday accommodation discount, subject to the program's rules, per CNA.
Other domestic tourism incentives include amusement park accommodation offers, corporate employee travel subsidies, and discounts on Taiwan PASS transportation packages.
The wider tourism promotion program also seeks to attract international visitors through incentives for repeat visits, travel associated with conventions and exhibitions, incentive group travel, and support for internationally recognized concerts.

Global poverty index rises for first time since its 2010 creation
Unknown
Unknown Publisher

13:45:00 KST

Global poverty index rises for first time since its 2010 creation
- The UNDP said the global poverty index rose for the first time since 2010, with 1.2 billion people now in “acute” poverty and 51.5 million more than last year.
- UNDP chief Alexander De Croo called this a “wake-up call for the world” and said poor people face hunger, missed schooling, and no clean water or electricity.
- The report said population growth helped drive the rise, but 33 countries cut poverty rates. Most of the poorest people still live in sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia.
AI generated
WASHINGTON – A UN global poverty index has risen for the first time since its creation in 2010, bringing the number of people affected to 1.2 billion, the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) reported on Oct 12.
In the 2026 edition of their annual report, the UNDP and the Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative research centre counted 51.5 million more people living in “acute” poverty compared to the previous year.
UNDP Administrator Alexander De Croo said the increase in poverty should be a “wake-up call for the world”.
“Behind these figures are 1.2 billion people facing hardships that reinforce one another: Hunger, missed schooling and a lack of clean water or electricity. This is unacceptable,” he said in a press release.
More than half of those in acute poverty were children.
However, UNDP said a major factor in the recorded increase was population growth, and new data was only available for 13 of the 108 developing countries covered by the report.
While the total number of people in poverty has increased, the report provides a mixed picture. Some 33 nations have halved the percentage of their people living in poverty as defined by the index in the past 15 years.
Those included six countries in sub-Saharan Africa. Among the countries that have made the most rapid progress were countries in Asia – China and Vietnam – UNDP said.
As in the previous year, the report found that the majority of the poorest people live in sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia, specifically the Indian subcontinent, the most densely populated region on Earth.
“In Egypt, Nepal, and Tajikistan, both the poverty rate and the number of people experiencing multidimensional poverty have decreased significantly,” the press release said.
In Angola and Zambia, the poverty rate has also declined, but population growth has more than offset this decrease, resulting in an increase in the number of people living in poverty.
The poverty index used in the report includes indicators such as the lack of adequate housing, sanitation, electricity, cooking fuel, food and education. AFP

Central Israel mayor, wife among 24 suspects in cash-for-contracts corruption probe; 17 arrested
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-12
04:43:15 UTC
13:43:15 KST

Police arrested 17 suspects, including Kfar Saba Mayor Rafi Saar, his wife and the CEO of the city's municipal economic development company, and detained seven others for questioning Monday in a sweeping corruption investigation involving alleged cash bribes, rigged tenders and ties to criminal figures. Officers from Lahav 433, Israel's national major crimes investigation unit, raided approximately 30 locations, including municipal offices, as an undercover investigation lasting nearly a year and a half became public.
Investigators suspect Saar and his wife promoted the interests of associates and businesspeople, including known criminal figures, in exchange for cash payments, helping them secure lucrative municipal contracts and projects. "The city was sold, nothing less than that," a source in the National Fraud Investigations Unit said, describing the suspected scale of the corruption.
Officials from the National Fraud Investigations Unit, part of Lahav 433, said the undercover investigation began in May 2025 after police received dozens of intelligence reports pointing to suspected widespread corruption at Kfar Saba City Hall, allegedly involving the mayor and his wife directly. According to investigators, although Saar's wife holds no official public position, she played a dominant and central role in the alleged scheme. "He is an elected official, she has no public standing, but she has a hand in everything," officials said.
During the covert investigation, detectives employed various investigative methods to substantiate their suspicions. According to information gathered, the couple allegedly worked to channel municipal tenders, properties and projects to associates, businesspeople and individuals with financial interests, some of whom are known to police as criminals. In return, investigators suspect Saar's wife received bundles of cash from those individuals, with whom she maintained direct contact.
The suspected method was straightforward: Businesspeople would approach the mayor's wife, establish a quid pro quo arrangement, and she would allegedly work to ensure they won municipal tenders and projects.
Police suspect that, to conceal preferential treatment of certain businesspeople and the alleged manipulation of tenders, projects were transferred from Kfar Saba City Hall to the municipal economic development company. Investigators believe the couple coordinated with the company's CEO, who allegedly knew in advance which bidder was supposed to win each tender brought before him.
Sources familiar with the investigation said detectives were surprised to discover that, in some cases, obstacles had allegedly been placed in the way of competing bidders until they were forced to withdraw. The projects were then allegedly awarded to businesspeople whose connections with the couple were suspected of benefiting them.
The allegations span nearly every area of municipal activity, including renovations of educational institutions, the placement of food trucks, the opening of businesses, the development of leisure and entertainment complexes, sports projects, transportation, traffic lights, street lighting and municipal cleaning services.
Another major element of the investigation concerns the couple's lifestyle and their allegedly extensive use of cash. According to National Fraud Investigations Unit officials, Saar and his wife maintained a lavish lifestyle, with numerous expenses paid in cash, including overseas travel, jewelry, clothing and handbags.
During police searches, investigators seized expensive jewelry and luxury watches, along with evidence of overseas flights and purchases. During the couple's most recent return from overseas, customs officials found 20,000 shekels in cash in Saar's wife's possession at Ben Gurion Airport, and she was questioned by customs authorities.
The couple also owned vehicles described by investigators as considerably more expensive than average. Saar drives a privately owned Tesla, while his wife recently purchased a new Audi.
"We are not investigating a technical violation involving the use of cash. If that were the issue, we would find a great many offenses of that kind," investigators explained, emphasizing that the cash transactions were being examined as part of the suspected bribery scheme.
During the police raids and searches, investigators discovered large quantities of cash, packaged and concealed in locations where detectives had anticipated finding it.
Investigators also revealed that Saar and his wife had grown increasingly concerned about the possibility that they were under surveillance. According to a source in the National Fraud Investigations Unit, rumors about the mayor's wife's influence over municipal affairs had circulated for some time, including reports in local newspapers suggesting that she effectively held the keys to running Kfar Saba.
The couple allegedly carried out technical checks to determine what surveillance methods might be used against them. Throughout the undercover investigation, they reportedly feared they were being monitored and investigated covertly.
"They had serious suspicions," the police source said. "There was a great deal of talk about the mayor's wife holding the key to running the city, and reports appeared in local newspapers. They conducted technical checks concerning measures that could be used against them. Throughout the investigation, they feared they were being monitored and investigated covertly. It sounded as though they believed they were the subject of a journalistic investigation, and they checked for devices that might have been installed but found nothing. Even so, their desire and sense of gratification blinded them."
Another line of investigation concerns suspected ties between Saar, his wife and criminal figures operating in the Sharon region. According to intelligence obtained by police, individuals known to the Israel Police's Central District for criminal activity allegedly helped Saar during the local election campaign.
Investigators suspect those individuals pressured political candidates running against Saar in an effort to influence the election. Police are examining the nature of the relationships between the criminal figures and the couple, as well as suspicions that those same individuals subsequently exerted pressure on the mayor and his wife.
The investigation centers on suspected bribery, fraud and breach of trust, with suspected money laundering and tax offenses also under examination. Among those arrested are businesspeople and individuals, some of whom are known to police for criminal activity. According to investigators, the common factor linking the suspects is their alleged involvement in quid pro quo arrangements in which financial interests were advanced in exchange for benefits.
Police said the investigation remains ongoing, with detectives examining the full scope of the suspected offenses and the alleged role of each individual involved. The case is being overseen by the Economic Department of the State Attorney's Office. Investigators are expected to seek extensions of detention for suspects where necessary at the Rishon LeZion Magistrate's Court.

The American message reportedly included threats to cut off intelligence sharing and suspend the mechanism through which Ukraine obtains U.S. weapons.
Among those contacted by U.S. officials was Zelensky's military adviser Pavlo Palisa, a former Ukrainian army general. One European official who spoke to the Financial Times said he had personally received a call from a U.S. defense official. "They're calling Kyiv, they're calling everyone in Europe," he said.
On Sunday, Trump announced that Russia and Ukraine had both agreed to an energy ceasefire under which neither side would attack the other's energy facilities. Neither country confirmed his announcement, and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky responded shortly afterward: "That's news to me."
Despite Trump's announcement, Russia struck power plants in Kharkiv and Kyiv on Sunday night, shortly after the purported ceasefire was supposed to take effect. "Our repair crews are only now restoring electricity and water supplies to Kyiv. Nobody has heard of a ceasefire," a senior Ukrainian official close to Zelensky told the Financial Times.

‘Find a new leader who can make a deal’
Trump called on Ukraine on Saturday to find a "new president" after Zelensky criticized a diesel agreement the American president had reached with Putin's Russia. The agreement would ease sanctions on Moscow and allow it to export diesel to countries around the world in an effort to ease shortages and curb rising prices. The deal drew sharp criticism from Ukraine and European governments, which warned that it would generate substantial revenue for Putin's government and help finance Russia's continued war against Ukraine.
Speaking to reporters at the White House, Trump was asked about Russian attacks on Ukraine, which have intensified recently and killed dozens more civilians in two particularly deadly strikes in recent days. Because he could have made a lot of deals, and for some reason he never does. This is a war that should never have started, and I think it's time for Ukraine to find a new president," Trump said.
For the past two years, Zelensky and his aides have repeatedly rejected the idea of holding elections while large numbers of Ukrainian refugees remain outside the country and Russia continues its attacks. His statement on Sunday that he would be willing to organize elections if Putin agreed to a 60-day ceasefire appears to signal an initial willingness to hold a vote even before the war ends. However, Zelensky likely knows that the Russian president is unlikely to accept such a condition.
Earlier, Zelensky also responded to Trump's demand that Ukraine stop attacking Russian oil refineries, which Kyiv has targeted in recent months. Those strikes caused a severe fuel crisis in Russia over the summer and forced Moscow, normally a major fuel exporter, to temporarily suspend diesel exports to preserve supplies for its own population. The disruption contributed to rising diesel prices, alongside increases driven by the war with Iran. For weeks, Trump has blamed Zelensky for rising global diesel prices, seeking to portray Ukraine, rather than the war with Iran, as the main cause of higher fuel costs burdening Americans ahead of next month's U.S. midterm elections.

Strikes on energy infrastructure could stop today, but Putin is not interested." He added that any step toward de-escalation must be reciprocal and backed by concrete guarantees. A few hours later, Trump announced that Russia and Ukraine had agreed to an immediate energy ceasefire, but neither side has formally confirmed such an agreement. Danish foreign minister warns US-Russia diesel deal could help finance war

Unknown Publisher
2026-10-12

13:30:37 KST

The Danish government has presented a proposed budget for 2027 that prioritizes national security, with more money allocated to defence amid an increasingly tense international security situation.
The proposal, titled “A stronger defence of Denmark – a strengthened Denmark to defend”, was presented by Finance Minister Peter Hummelgaard of the Social Democrats (S) at the Ministry of Finance on Friday morning.
The government wants to ensure that defence spending reaches 3.5 percent of gross domestic product (GDP) by 2030.
Hummelgaard said the proposal reflected the need to make “hard priorities” in response to the current security situation. He also described the Danish economy as being “in top shape”.
“The government’s proposal for the finance bill shows that we take responsibility upon ourselves, and that we lead the way in working for a greener, freer, and more equal Denmark,” Hummelgaard said.
Pia Olsen Dyhr of the Socialist People’s Party (SF), the minister for economic and interior affairs, also highlighted the security situation.
“We do not solve all the challenges we have in Denmark with this finance bill. But we are well on our way,” she said at the press conference.
“I also think everyone must remember that we are in an escalated security policy situation,” Olsen Dyhr said.
Much of the proposed budget had already been announced, either in the government’s policy platform or through statements by ministers in recent weeks.
The proposal allocates 1.2 billion DKK to children’s services and education in 2027, including Denmark’s public primary and lower secondary schools, known as folkeskole.
It also sets aside a total of 10.1 billion DKK in 2030 for tax cuts. These include abolishing the intermediate income tax and the top-top tax, as well as reducing corporation tax.
“We are simplifying the tax system,” said Taxation and Growth Minister Jakob Engel-Schmidt of the Moderates (M).
The tax measures will be negotiated separately as part of a tax reform. While the budget proposal includes tax cuts, the government also plans to freeze several tax thresholds, which would increase the tax burden for some taxpayers as incomes rise.
The liberal think tank Cepos estimates that the government’s various plans will result in a net tax cut of 2.2 billion DKK in 2030.
Business and Competitiveness Minister Martin Lidegaard of the Danish Social Liberal Party (R) highlighted investment in young people and education.
“We are significantly strengthening knowledge, general education, and formal education in Denmark, from ABC to PhD. It is good for the individual young person, but it is also good for Denmark’s future,” Lidegaard said.
Unlike in recent years, when the government’s fiscal room for manoeuvre helped fund much of its budget plans, this proposal includes several measures to find additional savings.
These include cuts to the Danish student grant (SU), savings on senior pension payments, a proposed tax on cruise ships and further reductions in state administration costs.
The government must now negotiate with other parties in the Danish Parliament, the Folketing, to secure a majority for the 2027 budget.
The proposal includes a negotiating reserve of 500 million DKK annually from 2027 to 2030, which other parties can seek to use to fund their own priorities.

04:30:32 UTC
13:30:32 KST

The Danish government has presented a proposed budget for 2027 that prioritizes national security, with more money allocated to defence amid an increasingly tense international security situation.
The proposal, titled “A stronger defence of Denmark – a strengthened Denmark to defend”, was presented by Finance Minister Peter Hummelgaard of the Social Democrats (S) at the Ministry of Finance on Friday morning.
The government wants to ensure that defence spending reaches 3.5 percent of gross domestic product (GDP) by 2030.
Hummelgaard said the proposal reflected the need to make “hard priorities” in response to the current security situation. He also described the Danish economy as being “in top shape”.
“The government’s proposal for the finance bill shows that we take responsibility upon ourselves, and that we lead the way in working for a greener, freer, and more equal Denmark,” Hummelgaard said.
Pia Olsen Dyhr of the Socialist People’s Party (SF), the minister for economic and interior affairs, also highlighted the security situation.
“We do not solve all the challenges we have in Denmark with this finance bill. But we are well on our way,” she said at the press conference.
“I also think everyone must remember that we are in an escalated security policy situation,” Olsen Dyhr said.
Much of the proposed budget had already been announced, either in the government’s policy platform or through statements by ministers in recent weeks.
The proposal allocates 1.2 billion DKK to children’s services and education in 2027, including Denmark’s public primary and lower secondary schools, known as folkeskole.
It also sets aside a total of 10.1 billion DKK in 2030 for tax cuts. These include abolishing the intermediate income tax and the top-top tax, as well as reducing corporation tax.
“We are simplifying the tax system,” said Taxation and Growth Minister Jakob Engel-Schmidt of the Moderates (M).
The tax measures will be negotiated separately as part of a tax reform. While the budget proposal includes tax cuts, the government also plans to freeze several tax thresholds, which would increase the tax burden for some taxpayers as incomes rise.
The liberal think tank Cepos estimates that the government’s various plans will result in a net tax cut of 2.2 billion DKK in 2030.
Business and Competitiveness Minister Martin Lidegaard of the Danish Social Liberal Party (R) highlighted investment in young people and education.
“We are significantly strengthening knowledge, general education, and formal education in Denmark, from ABC to PhD. It is good for the individual young person, but it is also good for Denmark’s future,” Lidegaard said.
Unlike in recent years, when the government’s fiscal room for manoeuvre helped fund much of its budget plans, this proposal includes several measures to find additional savings.
These include cuts to the Danish student grant (SU), savings on senior pension payments, a proposed tax on cruise ships and further reductions in state administration costs.
The government must now negotiate with other parties in the Danish Parliament, the Folketing, to secure a majority for the 2027 budget.
The proposal includes a negotiating reserve of 500 million DKK annually from 2027 to 2030, which other parties can seek to use to fund their own priorities.

Iran is currently developing more than 30 satellites and plans to begin rebuilding parts of its space industry damaged during the Ramadan War, Iranian Space Agency chief Hassan Salarieh said.
Speaking at a conference in Neyshabur, northeastern Iran, Salarieh said the country’s space industry is entirely domestic and relied on national capabilities.
“We are not concerned about damage to four [i.e., several] buildings,” he said, adding that reconstruction efforts would begin soon. He said countries perceived a serious capability as a threat, without elaborating further.
Salarieh also highlighted developments in Iran’s space program over the past two years, including space launches, the stabilization of the Simorgh satellite, the performance of the Nahid-2 satellite in orbit and the launch of three remote-sensing satellites.
He said the launches of the Paya, Zafar and Kowsar remote-sensing satellites marked the first private-sector launches in this field and demonstrated the rapid, competitive development of Iran’s space industry.
The space agency chief said further programs were planned for the coming months and that Iran expected to set new milestones in the sector.

Netanyahu demands probe into sources for award-winning Gaza film NAZA
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-12
04:24:18 UTC
13:24:18 KST

Netanyahu demands probe into sources for award-winning Gaza film NAZA
Documentary draws on 24 anonymous Israeli sources accusing military of killing Palestinians in Gaza using AI systems.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has called for an investigation into the anonymous sources featured in a documentary alleging that Israel’s military killed civilians in Gaza using AI-powered targeting systems.
The award-winning film, NAZA, draws on testimony from 24 unnamed Israeli military whistleblowers accusing the army of using the systems to kill numerous civilians in the besieged territory.
“I demand that the chief of general staff, the head of the Shin Bet, and the attorney general launch a comprehensive investigation into the participants in the film ‘Naza’ and prosecute them for serious information security violations, criminal libel, and harm to Israel’s diplomatic and security interests,” Netanyahu said on X on Saturday evening.
“The film presents a false, misleading, and biased narrative that defames the State of Israel and the [Israeli military] internationally, severely damaging Israel’s standing,” he added.
In a statement last month, the Israeli military said it “categorically” rejected the whistleblowers’ allegations, calling some of their assertions “absurd’ and contradictory.
It insisted that the selection and approval of strikes “are made by human personnel only”, in line with the military’s guidelines.
Israeli army Chief of Staff Eyal Zamir has called for legal action against the participants to be considered and ordered an investigation into suspected leaks of classified military information used in the film’s production.
NAZA takes its name from the Israeli military term for civilian casualties expected in air strikes, an abbreviated form of the Hebrew phrase for “collateral damage”.
The film was awarded a special jury prize at the Venice International Film Festival and received a historic 25-minute standing ovation.
It has also triggered a political storm in Israel.
The film’s directors, Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor, have been accused of “treason”. Netanyahu and Culture Minister Miki Zohar have threatened to revoke their Israeli citizenship.
Last week, the head of Israel’s National Public Diplomacy Directorate, Tzipi Hotovely, awarded the creators of another film, NAZA: The Real Story, certificates of recognition for countering the “blood libels” made in the original NAZA film.
According to a statement from the Prime Minister’s Office, NAZA: The Real Story features testimony from soldiers refuting the original claims.
In contrast, 43 Israeli rights groups defended the filmmakers of NAZA and denounced the threats being directed at them, according to Israel’s Channel 12 news.
Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza began on October 7, 2023, after Hamas’s armed wing, the Qassam Brigades, and other Palestinian groups attacked southern Israel, killing 1,139 people and taking about 240 captive.
Since then, Israel has killed at least 74,000 Palestinians, including at least 21,000 children, according to Gaza’s Ministry of Health.

Chinese desalination plant cuts 60% energy use, turns waste brine into industrial salt
Technology may help to solve the global problem of discharging concentrated by-products of drinking water production into the sea
3-MIN READ3-MIN
6
 Listen
Dannie Pengin Beijing
A large desalination plant on Bohai Bay has achieved an energy efficiency breakthrough, slashing electricity consumption by more than half while converting millions of tonnes of toxic waste brine into high-value chemical salt.
Situated in the Caofeidian industrial zone of Tangshan, Hebei province, the facility recently entered its trial production stage, the state-run Science and Technology Daily reported last month.
This technology provides a viable pathway to solving the global challenge of discharging concentrated seawater into the sea, according to the report.
The facility processes waste brine at a three-to-one ratio, yielding 1 tonne of refined concentrated seawater – with a salinity of 120 grams per litre – alongside 2 tonnes of fresh water.

Roti Jala: a golden net of Malaysian culture on Tehran’s guest table
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-12
04:14:59 UTC
13:14:59 KST

Roti Jala: a golden net of Malaysian culture on Tehran’s guest table
TEHRAN — The Embassy of Malaysia in Tehran on Sunday, October 11, hosted a warm and colorful gathering in which the aroma of Malay spices and hospitality, leaving a lasting memory of friendship between two cultures.
The event brought together foreign diplomats, officials from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Iran, Iranian graduates of Malaysian universities, and alumni of the Malaysian Technical Cooperation Program (MTCP). At its heart was one of Malaysia’s most beloved culinary treasures: roti jala.
At the beginning of the ceremony, Dato’ Wan Aznainizam Yusri bin Wan Abdul Rashid, Chargé d’Affaires and Head of Mission at the Embassy of Malaysia, delivered this speech:
“Distinguished guests,
Officials from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Islamic Republic of Iran as well as other agencies, fellow diplomats, dear friends of Malaysia,
Ladies and gentlemen, good afternoon, and a very warm welcome — khosh amadeh — to the Embassy of Malaysia.
Thank you all for taking the time to join us today. Your presence reflects the strong bonds of friendship and cooperation that our nations, and indeed our diplomatic communities, continue to enjoy.
Today’s gathering serves a wonderful dual purpose. First and foremost, it is my distinct pleasure to officially introduce the Embassy’s new Head of Chancery, Mr. Muhammad Shahiran. Shahiran joined our team in Tehran a couple of weeks ago with a wealth of experience, having been posted previously in Turkmenistan and Peru. I know he is eager to get to know all of you, and I am confident he will find the same warmth, kindness, and cooperation from the officials here, the diplomatic community, as well as the Friends of Malaysia in Iran that I have enjoyed since my arrival last August. Please join me in welcoming him to his new home in Iran!
Mr. Muhammad Shahiran
Our second objective today is to share a piece of Malaysian culture with you through one of our greatest passions: our food.
The great Persian poet Rumi once beautifully captured the magic of gathering around food to feed the soul:
‘Sof-reh bee-aa-reed o fo-rood aa-va-reed’
‘Peesh ka-shee-dash keh kam lar-zand mo-reed’
‘Bring out the table spread, set it down, and bring the food,
For the lovers must be fed.’
Malaysia is known globally as a food paradise, where our diverse culture is reflected directly on our plates. Today, as part of our ongoing cultural diplomacy and efforts to promote Malaysia’s rich heritage, our Home-Based Staff have put together a special culinary showcase. Shortly, you will witness a live cooking demonstration of Roti Jala — which translates to ‘Net Bread’ due to its intricate, lace-like design. This traditional favourite is paired perfectly with our classic chicken and beef curries, rich with aromatic spices that I believe will resonate deeply with the sophisticated palates of our Iranian friends.
I would not want to take much of the time to bore you with my long speech. Let’s skip the formalities today. Enjoy the cooking demonstration, eat heartily, and let the food do what it does best — bring us closer together.
Thank you all very much, and kheyli mamnoon.”
After the speech, embassy staff demonstrated the art of making roti jala with skill and delicacy: a thin batter poured through a special funnel into fine, lace-like webs on the pan, turning in moments into golden, netted bread. Guests were also given the chance to try their own hand at it, shaping the batter and joyfully eating what they had made. A tahari — a spread of diverse Malaysian dishes — was then served, from aromatic curries to beloved Malay favorites, transforming the embassy into a small corner of Kuala Lumpur. Guests mingled, chatted, and deepened their friendships in the warm atmosphere.
And it was the incomparable hospitality of Dato’ Wan Aznainizam Yusri bin Wan Abdul Rashid and the Malaysian embassy team that made the pleasure of this gathering doubly memorable — a warmth felt from the very first moment and lingering, like the scent of Malay spices, long after the last bite. Roti Jala today was not merely a bread; it was a net that wove cultures together and proved that food is the most eloquent language of friendship among nations.
Photos by Niloofar Aghili

India’s agri-seed sector accounts for the largest share of receipts under benefit sharing regulations during April-Sept
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-12
04:04:52 UTC
13:04:52 KST

ABS mechanism goes beyond monetary collection by linking the utilisation of biological resources with biodiversity conservation,
NEW DELHI: India’s agri-seed sector accounted for the largest share of receipts from users of the country’s biological resources during April-Sept period this financial year under the Access and Benefit Sharing (ABS) regulation -- a statutory mechanism which ensures that when local genetic resources create commercial value, a fair share flows back to states and communities to sustain that diversity.Though the amount of little over Rs 7 crore for the sector during that six-month period is not much, the receipts, at least, reflect working of the ABS mechanism in generating money by getting payment for utilisation of a diverse range of biological resources across agriculture sector.The other sectors that generate receipts include food, pharmaceuticals, biotechnology, medicinal plants, microorganisms and livestock. A total of around Rs 9.6 crore was received by the National Biodiversity Authority (NBA) towards access to biological resources from users in various sectors during the period.Contributions were received by the NBA from both domestic and international entities, including companies from Sri Lanka, Germany, France, the Republic of Korea and Bhutan.Union environment ministry’s records show that the NBA has realised around Rs 278 crore through ABS and disbursed more than Rs 200 crore towards biodiversity conservation and benefits for communities, farmers, institutions and other benefit claimers across the country since 2008.
The Authority, a statutory body under the Biological Diversity Act, 2002, regulates access to India's biological resources and associated knowledge and implements the Nagoya Protocol’s (a global convention) principle of fair and equitable sharing of benefits.Biological resources, used by different entities for developing seeds, include livestock genetic resources such as Mithun, Jersey cattle and frozen semen of Murrah buffalo, as well as Red Sanders wood sourced from cultivated sources and auctioned material. The range further includes agricultural crops such as chickpea, red lentil, green moong, horse gram, flaxseed, guar gum, tapioca, buckwheat, brown rice, cauliflower, okra, hot pepper, brinjal and ridge gourd.The biological resources also include medicinal plants such as Ashwagandha, Shatavari, Kalmegh, Vasaka, Licorice, Arjuna, Bacopa, Gotukola and Moringa, as well as soil microorganisms including Azospirillum, Azotobacter, Bacillus, Rhizobium, Trichoderma and Metarhizium.The ABS mechanism goes beyond monetary collection by linking the utilisation of biological resources with biodiversity conservation, sustainable use and equitable sharing of benefits.“Funds disbursed through the State Biodiversity Boards and Union Territory Biodiversity Councils support conservation of biological resources, preparation and updation of People's Biodiversity Registers, strengthening of Biodiversity Management Committees, biodiversity research and documentation, and benefits to local communities and other benefit claimers,” said the Union environment ministry on working of the mechanism and utilisation of the collected money.ABS-funded activities can complement relevant govt schemes and programmes, particularly those promoting tribal welfare, sustainable livelihoods and natural-resource-based enterprises, such as the Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan (PM-JANMAN), Pradhan Mantri Janjatiya Vikas Mission and Pradhan Mantri Van Dhan Yojana.“Such convergence can strengthen community-led conservation, sustainable utilisation of biological resources and livelihood opportunities, while leveraging existing institutional mechanisms,” said the ministry in a statement.India’s ABS framework supports Target 13 of the Kunming–Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework on the fair and equitable sharing of benefits arising from the utilisation of genetic resources and associated traditional knowledge, as well as Target 19 on resource mobilisation. The framework also contributes to relevant Sustainable Development Goals, including SDG 2 (Zero Hunger), SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth), SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production), SDG 15 (Life on Land) and SDG 17 (Partnerships for the Goals), through biodiversity conservation, sustainable resource use, livelihood support and institutional collaboration.
“As India prepares to participate in the seventeenth meeting of the Conference of the Parties to the Convention on Biological Diversity (COP 17), commencing on 19 October 2026 in Yerevan, Armenia, its ABS framework demonstrates the country’s continued commitment to biodiversity conservation, the sustainable use of biological resources and the fair and equitable sharing of benefits arising from their utilisation,” said the ministry.
Vishwa Mohan is Senior Editor at The Times of India. He writes on environment, climate change, agriculture, water resources and clean energy, tracking policy issues and climate diplomacy. He has been covering Parliament since 2003 to see how politics shaped up domestic policy and India’s position at global platform. Before switching over to explore sustainable development issues, Vishwa had covered internal security and investigative agencies for more than a decade.

Ukraine’s external debt repayments to total $4.86 billion in 2026
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-12
04:03:29 UTC
13:03:29 KST

MOSCOW, October 12. /TASS/. In 2026, Ukraine will repay $4.86 billion in a total debt to its foreign creditors, calculations by TASS based on data from Ukraine’s Finance Ministry showed.
Principal debt repayments will amount to €490 million ($550 million), $600 million and 1.26 billion in IMF Special Drawing Rights (XDR) ($1.7 billion, bringing the total to $2.41 billion. Interest payments will include €220 million ($246.6 million), $970 million, 40 million sterling pounds ($52.90 million), and 0.56 billion XDR ($756 million), or a total of $2.45 billion.
As of August 31, the country’s state and state-guaranteed debt stood at 9.603 trillion hryvnias, or $215.55 billion. According to calculations by TASS, every Ukrainian citizen owes his country $8,622, given the nation has a population of 25 million and a public debt of $215.55 billion. If calculations are based on a population of 22 million, the national debt amounts to nearly $9,800 per person. While there are no accurate population numbers for Ukraine, the country’s Social Policy Minister Denis Ulyutin earlier mentioned population figures of between 22 million and 25 million.

North Korea fires multiple ballistic missiles towards the sea
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-12
03:37:12 UTC
12:37:12 KST

North Korea fires multiple ballistic missiles towards the sea
South Korea’s Joint Chiefs of Staff said one of the missiles launched from the Pyongyang area flew more than 900km.
North Korea has fired multiple ballistic missiles towards the sea off its east coast, South Korea’s military says.
South Korea’s Joint Chiefs of Staff (JCS) said one of the missiles launched from the Pyongyang area flew more than 900km (559 miles) on Monday. The joint chiefs did not specify how many missiles were detected.
Japan’s Deputy Defence Minister Takashi Koyari said at least two missiles were launched 17 minutes apart and landed in waters outside of its exclusive economic zone.
Koyari said the first missile flew about 220 kilometres (137 miles) and the second more than 910 kilometres (565 miles), following an “irregular” flight path and suggested it may have been a hypersonic weapon.
South Korea’s presidential office said that Pyongyang’s repeated missile launches violate United Nations Security Council resolutions, urging an immediate stop.
Monday’s launches add to heightened tensions on the Korean Peninsula, as both countries have been conducting weapons tests.
Escalating tensions
JCS spokesperson Jang Do-young said the latest missile launch appears to be a show of force, days after South Korea tested its own hypersonic weapon.
On Thursday, South Korean President Lee Jae Myung oversaw the country’s first test-firing of a hypersonic missile, a rare public showcasing of a missile test by a South Korean president.
Lee’s office said the hypersonic weapon, once fully developed, would enhance South Korea’s ability to strike key targets by surprise in the “Korean Peninsula theatre of operations”.
On October 3, North Korea also tested a hypersonic intermediate-range missile designed to evade missile defences in South Korea and Japan.
Last week, Seoul demanded an apology after a landmine blast wounded three soldiers in the Demilitarized Zone between South and North Korea. A joint South Korean-UN investigation concluded that two landmines were planted by North Korean forces about a year ago. Pyongyang dismissed the claim and accused South Korea of provocation.
Prior to the border mine blast, Seoul said it was conducting “preliminary coordination efforts” to facilitate dialogue between Pyongyang and Washington.
Lee pledged to reopen dialogue with North Korea in his first speech after taking office in 2025.
North Korean leader Kim Jong Un continues to flaunt his nuclear weapons programme, while rejecting US and South Korean offers to resume stalled diplomacy.
Talks between Kim and United States President Donald Trump abruptly ended in 2019. Kim Jong Un’s government continues to demand that Washington abandon its “hostile” policy towards Pyongyang and drop demands for North Korea’s denuclearisation as a condition for talks.

The first travellers to pass through the redeveloped Huanggang port on its first day of operation have praised its convenience.
The new facility opened at 6.30am on Monday, providing 24-hour clearance services for passengers and passenger vehicles.
One traveller from the Shenzhen side said it was spacious, comfortable and very convenient.
“I came early just to try it out," she said. "It feels very big and comfortable. You get off the Shenzhen metro, go up two levels, and you're through – it's very convenient.” 
Another woman praised its enhanced connectivity, with more bus services reaching different districts in the SAR.
“We have more choices now, with buses and minibuses,” she said.
“There are also many new routes. In the past, we could only go to Kowloon or Hong Kong Island after crossing Huanggang port, but now there are routes to Tai Po and Ma On Shan, as well as to the airport. It is convenient for people arriving in Hong Kong.”
From the Hong Kong side, a traveller said the new checkpoint made it more convenient for her to visit Shenzhen and other mainland cities, adding it would be her first choice for future border crossings.
“I used to cross over using Lo Wu checkpoint, but the fare to get there is more expensive than coming to Huanggang port,” she said. 
"Also, the new facility is very convenient with many buses coming here.
A man said it only took him around 20 minutes to reach the checkpoint from Tsing Yi, putting the new facility within easy reach.
Some travellers also drove over, and feng shui master Mak Ling-ling was one of them.
“The operation of the port was smooth," she said. 
"As for the time required, the redeveloped port has more lanes than before so the process was faster.” 
Mak said the clearance procedure took less than a minute, making it a pleasant experience.

U.S. judge orders halt to taxpayer-funded Trump ads
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-12
11:19:47 CST
12:19:47 KST

WASHINGTON, Oct. 11 (Xinhua) -- A U.S. federal judge on Sunday ordered the Trump administration to immediately halt any remaining taxpayer-funded television ads promoting President Donald Trump, including those scheduled to air later that evening.
U.S. District Judge Jennifer L. Rochon in New York issued a temporary restraining order after siding with a coalition of plaintiffs, including the nonpartisan watchdog Common Cause, who challenged the ads as an illegal misuse of public funds, according to local media reports.
The ruling came as the Trump administration said its advertising campaign, which had cost approximately 19 million U.S. dollars in taxpayer funds, was set to end Sunday.
The Democratic National Committee (DNC) on Wednesday sued the Trump administration over what it described as campaign-style television advertisements, accusing the administration of using taxpayer funds in violation of federal laws.
The DNC lawsuit, filed in the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia, listed the president, the White House Office, the Office of Management and Budget and the U.S. Department of Homeland Security as defendants.
In late September, advertisements began to appear on broadcast television, touting Trump and his midterm messaging, including one which is virtually identical to a 2024 campaign ad, according to the complaint. The complaint noted that each advertisement ends with the statement "Paid for by the U.S. Government." ■

India condemns attacks on commercial vessels in Strait of Hormuz region
China
Unknown Publisher

11:19:10 CST

NEW DELHI, Oct. 12 (Xinhua) -- India's External Affairs Ministry on Sunday condemned the recent attacks on two ships, MT Petro Dolphin and MT Valthera, in the Strait of Hormuz region, which left two Indian seafarers missing.
In an official statement, the ministry said that such attacks must cease, and called for an unimpeded flow of maritime commerce through international waterways.
There were 11 Indian seafarers on MT Petro Dolphin when it came under a drone attack. While 9 were rescued safely, two were still missing. The other set of 11 Indians aboard MT Valthera were said to be safe after the vessel was struck by an unknown projectile, according to the statement.
The ministry further stated that the recurring attacks on commercial shipping in the region were deeply concerning, and risked further aggravating an already volatile situation, adding that freedom of navigation and the safe, unimpeded flow of maritime commerce through international waterways, in accordance with international law, must be upheld. ■

Netanyahu's election gamble: Team up with Smotrich, take votes from Ben-Gvir
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-12
03:16:04 UTC
12:16:04 KST

After four years together in government, cooperation between Likud and Religious Zionism continues to deepen ahead of the upcoming elections. The parties have launched a joint campaign to "save the right-wing bloc," with the central goal of strengthening and expanding their political power.
Sources in both parties say personal ties between their leaders, Benjamin Netanyahu and Bezalel Smotrich, have also grown closer during the past term, particularly following Itamar Ben-Gvir's temporary withdrawal from the government over the hostage deal, while the finance minister remained loyal and paid a political price for doing so.
The strengthening alliance includes several measures: establishing a joint field campaign headquarters; mobilizing hundreds of activists, both volunteers and paid staff, to work on behalf of both parties; jointly mapping potential voter groups to increase turnout and maximize electoral opportunities; and preparing a detailed, coordinated schedule for Election Day.
The joint field campaign headquarters was recently established under the leadership of Yesha Council Chairman Yisrael Gantz, representing Likud, and Yesha Council Director-General Omer Rahamim, representing Smotrich.
The two are analyzing previous election results, identifying areas with untapped voting potential and working to significantly increase turnout in those cities.
With the help of numerous campaign workers and volunteers, they are dividing areas of responsibility among activists and plan to go door to door on Election Day to encourage people to vote and ensure that as many potential supporters of both parties as possible cast their ballots. The joint operation aims to help voters reach polling stations, including providing transportation when necessary.
Beyond their field operations, Likud and Religious Zionism also are cooperating on the parliamentary front, having signed a vote-sharing agreement.
"On the one hand, Likud and Religious Zionism appeal to different audiences, so their messages are also different," a source in Smotrich's party said. "On the other hand, we're all coming together for one goal: forming a broad coalition and winning the election."
Failed efforts to forge a broader alliance
Last week, Smotrich held his first major Religious Zionism conference, attended by yeshiva heads, rabbis, prominent activists and members of his grassroots communities.
He invited Netanyahu, who immediately confirmed his attendance to project a united front. During the conference, the two sat side by side and appeared closely coordinated.
This was particularly noticeable when it emerged that Itamar Ben-Gvir, their fellow member of the right-wing bloc, had not been invited to the event at all.
The national security minister also has complained that the prime minister refuses to be photographed near him or appear alongside him at public events.
As cooperation between Likud and Religious Zionism intensifies, the growing distance from Ben-Gvir has become increasingly apparent.
Officials in both parties blame Ben-Gvir, arguing that he has deliberately isolated himself.
Likud officials believe that while Shas and Religious Zionism are playing a coordinated bloc-wide game, the national security minister is pursuing a personal political strategy focused solely on his own success.
"Ben-Gvir wants to grow at Likud's expense, and that's what his entire campaign looks like," a senior Likud official said. "He isn't cooperating on anything related to winning the election for the bloc. He barely focuses on messages against the opposition and instead highlights internal conflicts within the bloc. He's deliberately creating a situation in which he is left out. That's his campaign."
Netanyahu's party says it held several discussions with representatives of Otzma Yehudit about cooperation, but claims Ben-Gvir showed no willingness to participate, either operationally or financially.
Because of that lack of cooperation, Likud officials believe many of the seats currently projected for Ben-Gvir in the polls represent voters whose support remains uncertain. They intend to try to win those voters back ahead of the election.
The Defense Ministry at the center of the dispute
Relations between Likud and Otzma Yehudit have become even more strained recently following Ben-Gvir's new campaign, which declared that "if Ben-Gvir had been defense minister, October 7 would not have happened."
The national security minister's coalition partners viewed the statement as provocative and interpreted it as further evidence that Ben-Gvir was focused on strengthening his party at their expense. This, in turn, further reinforced the Netanyahu-Smotrich alliance.
Likud's assessment is that Ben-Gvir is the only figure in Netanyahu's bloc competing directly for the same voters as the party. As a result, a political battle has developed between Likud and Otzma Yehudit over a large pool of undecided right-wing voters.
Throughout the recent period, Ben-Gvir's office has maintained that his support for Netanyahu is unconditional. In practice, however, from Ben-Gvir's perspective, the contest on the right is no longer about who will be prime minister, but rather who will serve as Netanyahu's defense minister.
Ben-Gvir has publicly identified the Defense Ministry as his next political goal.
Netanyahu understands that to prevent Ben-Gvir from achieving that ambition and force him to lower his expectations, he must weaken Otzma Yehudit and reduce the number of seats it wins in the election.
"Instead of directing his energy outward, Ben-Gvir is creating a situation in which the election is being fought within the right-wing bloc: Either Netanyahu or Ben-Gvir. That's completely unreasonable," a Religious Zionism source said.
"For two months, Smotrich talked about cooperation and coordination within the bloc. He wanted everyone together, but Winter and Ben-Gvir decided to go it alone. That's part of what led to the closer relationship with Likud."

Saudi Arabia, Israel have shared interests at stake, Houthi escalation highlights - editorial
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-12
03:14:19 UTC
12:14:19 KST

A strike by Houthi terrorists on the international airport in the Saudi capital, Riyadh, has turned the desert kingdom’s efforts to mobilize security partners into an immediate test: Can new and existing ties protect the kingdom without widening the conflict? The attack killed 12 people and wounded an additional 309, according to Saudi civil aviation authorities. The Houthis have since warned airlines, passengers, and airport workers to avoid Saudi airports and airspace.
The consequences extend beyond the casualties. Riyadh’s airport remained closed on Sunday, and airlines canceled or suspended flights after the Houthis warned that Saudi airspace had become a theater of military operations. The October 10 strike was the third attack on the airport that week. Earlier attacks there killed three people, including a Saudi pilot. The Houthis have also threatened Saudi energy facilities.
The escalation is pulling Saudi Arabia back into a war it had spent years trying to contain. A 2022 truce between the Houthis and Saudi Arabia largely held until fighting resumed in July. Since then, the Houthis have advanced along Yemen’s Red Sea coast. At the same time, forces fighting on behalf of the internationally recognized government of Yemen have launched a counteroffensive with Saudi air support and other military backing.
The internationally recognized Yemeni government says its forces have retaken strategic positions near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait; the Houthis dispute those claims, and the extent of the government’s gains remains unclear. The coalition’s spokesman said 100 aircraft took part in the operation and claimed 324 high-value targets were destroyed; neither claim has been independently verified as of Sunday.
The Houthis have claimed control of territory and islands near the strait, including Perim Island, while government forces say they have pushed back.
Bab el-Mandeb connects the Gulf of Aden to the Red Sea and the Suez Canal. The Houthis’ positions near the strait give them greater ability to monitor and threaten shipping, though they do not control the passage in a way that lets them stop all traffic. Riyadh must protect its cities and energy infrastructure while backing a campaign to regain ground along a vital maritime route.
Saudi Arabia’s response presents a difficult choice. Restraint could leave the kingdom’s airspace exposed and weaken the deterrent message of its new partnerships. A deeper campaign could prolong the fighting and put Saudi forces and their partners at greater risk.
Saudi defense pact with Turkey, Pakistan faces test amid Houthi escalation
The Mecca Joint Defense Agreement with Turkey and Pakistan is one part of that calculation. The three countries signed it in August. On October 5, their joint committee said it would begin implementing collective-defense commitments and provide agreed military capabilities for rapid deployment in Saudi Arabia. The public statement did not identify the forces involved or give a timetable, leaving open how the commitment would work in practice.
Turkey has described the pact as defensive. Reuters reported, citing officials, that Turkish support would be mainly technical and defensive. The announcement left operational questions unanswered, including the size and command of any deployment. It is too early to judge what the agreement will deliver or whether either partner will join the fighting in Yemen. A collective-defense commitment does not itself establish participation in offensive operations.
Houthi threat to Red Sea shipping raises concerns for Israel's Eilat port
For Israel, the most immediate connection is the vulnerability of Red Sea shipping. Houthi attacks have kept international shipping lines from returning to regular direct sailings to Eilat. Recent advances near Bab el-Mandeb have renewed concern about the port’s recovery. Some activity has resumed through cargo unloaded in Aqaba, Jordan, but the direct route has not returned. The threat to shipping is already an Israeli economic and security concern, whether or not Saudi Arabia and Israel expand their contacts.
Israeli media have separately reported that Israel has provided or discussed intelligence assistance to Saudi Arabia through US Central Command. Those accounts rely on regional diplomatic or security sources; neither government has publicly confirmed the details. They do not establish a formal alliance or Israeli participation in the fighting.
The Riyadh strike is an early test of Saudi Arabia’s emerging security network. The broader question is whether Riyadh can protect its cities and trade routes while reversing Houthi gains without turning the renewed campaign into a deeper regional war. For Israel, the consequences will also be felt in terms of the safety and viability of the Red Sea routes on which Eilat depends.

North Korea launches multiple ballistic missiles, South Korea says
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-12
03:14:15 UTC
12:14:15 KST

North Korea fired multiple ballistic missiles toward the sea off its east coast on Monday, South Korea's military said, marking Pyongyang'sfourth launch in a month and following Seoul's recent test of a hypersonic missile.
The ballistic missiles, which appeared to be of different types, were fired at around 9:20 a.m. local time from near Pyongyang, and one type flew more than 900 km, South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff said.
Earlier, Japan's coast guard said North Korea had fired two unidentified projectiles, believed to be ballistic missiles, adding that both appeared to have already fallen.
South Korea's National Security Office convened an emergency meeting, where it condemned the missile launches as violations of United Nations Security Council resolutions and urged an immediate stop.
North Korea has been under UN sanctions since 2006, aimed at halting Pyongyang's development of nuclear weapons and ballistic missiles.
South Korea tests hypersonic missile
The latest launches come at a time when tensions have been rising between the two Koreas in recent weeks amid weapons tests by both countries.
Last week, South Korean President Lee Jae Myung oversaw the country's first test-firing of a hypersonic missile, a rare public showcasing of a missile test by a South Korean president.
Monday's missile launches by North Korea appeared to be "a show of force in response to the successful test launch of our hypersonic missile, as well as an intentional demonstration of missile capabilities," a spokesperson for South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff said.
North Korea last fired a ballistic missile on October 3, with state media KCNA saying it was a hypersonic missile tested under the supervision of leader Kim Jong Un.
The tests followed a border mine blast last month that wounded three South Korean soldiers. Seoul said the landmines had been planted by North Korea and demanded an apology, but Pyongyang has dismissed this and accused South Korea of provocation.
Pyongyang has conducted missile tests on more than 10 occasions this year, including four in the last month.
The unusually frequent tests suggest Pyongyang wanted to increase its leverage ahead of a potential summit between leader Kim and US President Donald Trump, said Song Seong-jong, a professor at Daejeon University in Seoul and a former official at South Korea's Defense Ministry.
"They definitely need to raise the value of their status before meeting Trump," Song said.
